about.title: About Power Converter
about.description: The Power Converter provides conversion between different power units including watts, kilowatts, horsepower, BTU/hour, and other power measurements. It is useful for engineers, electricians, HVAC work, and anyone comparing electrical, mechanical, and thermal power calculations. Understanding power unit conversions helps in electrical-system planning, motor specifications, generator sizing, and energy-efficiency checks across industrial, automotive, and residential applications. Whether you're sizing electrical equipment, comparing motor ratings, or calculating heating-system capacity, our converter helps compare major power units using standard conversion factors.

faq.q: What's the difference between watts and horsepower for power measurement?
faq.a: Watts are the SI (International System) unit for power used in electrical and scientific applications, while horsepower is a traditional unit commonly used for mechanical power, especially in automotive and industrial motors. 1 horsepower equals exactly 745.7 watts. Our power converter handles both units with precise calculations for all applications.

faq.q: How do I convert kilowatts to horsepower?
faq.a: 1 kilowatt equals approximately 1.341 horsepower. To convert kilowatts to horsepower, multiply the kW value by 1.341. For example, 10 kW = 13.41 horsepower. Our power converter performs this calculation automatically with full precision.

faq.q: What are BTU/hour units used for in power calculations?
faq.a: BTU/hour (British Thermal Units per hour) measures thermal power output, commonly used in heating and cooling system specifications, furnace capacity ratings, and air conditioning unit sizing. 1 BTU/hr equals approximately 0.293 watts.

faq.q: Which power unit should I use for different applications?
faq.a: Use watts and kilowatts for electrical power calculations and equipment specifications, horsepower for mechanical power and motor ratings, BTU/hr for heating and cooling system capacity, and foot-pounds per second for mechanical power in imperial systems.

faq.q: How accurate is the power converter for engineering use?
faq.a: Our power converter uses exact international conversion factors and maintains high decimal precision, making it suitable for electrical-system planning, motor sizing, generator specifications, and engineering reference calculations.

faq.q: Can I convert between electrical and mechanical power units?
faq.a: Yes, our power converter accurately converts between electrical power (watts, kW) and mechanical power (horsepower) using precise conversion factors. This is essential for motor selection, generator sizing, and power system analysis.
